newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia's Meles vows war on Islamic group.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia's Meles vows war on Islamic group.

text.p: Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi vowed on Saturday to hunt down the Al-Ittihad Al-Islam (Islamic Unity) unless the Somali fundamentalist group stopped attacks on Ethiopia.
"We have made it abundantly clear that unless they (Al-Ittihad) stop their attempt to destabilise Ethiopia, we will hunt them down and hit them wherever they are," Meles told a news conference.
The Islamic fundamentalist group is suspected by the Addis Ababa government of bomb attacks on soft targets, like hotels, during the past two years.
"Al-Ittihad is a terrorist front not necessarily a purely Somali group. It is a group in which many so-called Arab Africans are involved," Meles said.
Denying Ethiopia was involved in a recent battle inside Somalia, he said he was certain Al-Ittihad wanted to terrorise Ethiopia, Somalia and the region.
Aid and security sources in Nairobi said earlier this month Ethiopian troops and Somali militia allies were in full control of an area inside Somalia after driving Al-Ittihad out of a stronghold.
Ethiopian forces backed Omar Haji's Somali National Front (SNF) during a lightning offensive to capture the towns of Luq and Bulo Hawo in Gedo region, the sources said.

Al-Ittihad set up its headquarters in Somalia's Luq in 1992, a year after central government collapsed in the Horn of Africa country. Since 1991 Somalia has drifted through civil war and anarchy although most of the country is now relatively peaceful. There is no unified army to protect frontiers.
